title: Osmosis and water potential; Active transport, bulk transport and co-transport
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: MB03b#t2 term and clue written for the game; MB03b#t1 term and clue written for the game; MB04#t2 term and clue written for the game; MB04#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: MB03b#N.5, MB04#N.3b, MB03b#N.7, MB04#N.8b.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Percentage change
items.clue: Final mass minus initial mass, divided by initial mass, times 100.

items.label: Dilution series
items.clue: Set of sucrose solutions of different strengths made from one stock solution.

items.label: Respiratory inhibitor
items.clue: Substance that cuts a cell's ATP supply, so uptake against a gradient falls sharply.

items.label: Active transport
items.clue: Uptake needing ATP and a membrane protein, able to build a substance up above the outside concentration.

questions.stem: A cell from a hypothetical plant has sucrose as the solute in its cell sap, at a concentration of 0.20 M, at a temperature of 27 °C. Its pressure potential is +2.0 bars. Using Ψ = ΨP + ΨS and ΨS = −iCRT, where R = 0.0831 liter bars/mole K, what is the water potential of the cell?
questions.explanation: ΨS = −(1.0)(0.20)(0.0831)(300) = −5.0 bars; adding the pressure potential gives Ψ = +2.0 + (−5.0) = −3.0 bars.

questions.stem: Cells of a hypothetical seaweed accumulate iodide ions (I⁻) to a concentration many times higher than that in the seawater around them. Which statement best explains why the cells must use metabolic energy, such as energy from ATP, to do this?

options.text: Iodide stops moving once its concentrations inside and outside match, so energy restarts it.
Moving iodide from lower to higher concentration is not spontaneous, so it needs energy.
Energy is needed just once, to set up the iodide gradient, which then stays in place without it.
The cells need iodide, and any substance a cell needs must be taken in using ATP.

questions.stem: A student fills bags of dialysis tubing, which is permeable to water but not to sucrose, with 0.2 M, 0.4 M or 0.6 M sucrose solution and places each bag in a beaker of distilled water. The percent change in mass of each bag is measured after 30 minutes. To show that the mass changes are caused by the sucrose concentration inside the bags, and not by the tubing itself absorbing water, which additional set-up is needed?

options.text: An empty bag of tubing that is kept dry outside any beaker
A bag of distilled water placed in a beaker of distilled water
A bag of 1.0 M sucrose solution placed in distilled water
The same three bags, weighed again after a further 30 minutes in water

questions.stem: In a hypothetical animal cell, a drug blocks the Na⁺/K⁺ pump (Na⁺/K⁺ ATPase) but has no direct effect on any ion channel. Which prediction about the cell during the following hour is best supported?

options.text: The membrane potential gradually shrinks, as Na⁺ and K⁺ leak through channels and their gradients run down.
The membrane potential drops to zero at once, as the pump by itself produces all of the potential.
The Na⁺ and K⁺ gradients stay as they are, as gradients need energy just to be built, not kept.
Ion channels take over, moving Na⁺ out and K⁺ in against their gradients as the pump did.
